title: Dale
type: Centaur musician; protector and reluctant leader
imageAlt: Dale playing a small stringed instrument
dek: A centaur musician who sings courage into defenders, helps refugees find food and shelter, and meets danger with loyalty, jokes and occasional confusion.

facts.Pattern: Enjoy → accept the absurdity → protect friends

body:
Dale sings courage into defenders and notices bowls, spoons, lumber, shelter, and the need to ask displaced people what they actually want. He is easy to underestimate because the same history also remembers a shark transformation, a successful attempt to hide behind a potted plant, and private relief when directions spare him from revealing trouble with left and right.

The comedy does not make danger fake. Dale remains himself while consequences are real, and his apparently simple reasoning often reaches the emotional truth faster than more elaborate philosophies: a friend is in danger, so help the friend.

A courteous centaur and a reluctant leader

The earliest recovered introduction places Dale on a water and disease investigation on 6 May 2024. He makes room for others, introduces himself with “Howdy! I'm Dale,” and brings music and encouragement to a company he is still learning to belong to.

On 5 June he doubts his ability to lead, even after the company completes its mission and seals a dangerous cave. Olokun and Wren recognize the result: the mission succeeded and nobody died. Dale’s leadership grows through responsibility for particular people, rather than confidence in a title.

The first death and return

After the early July expedition, Elenia begins the work of restoring Dale with a diamond. The Tower scene posted on 9 July records the outcome: his burns heal, his heart starts again and he wakes beside Saray. His first words apologize for worrying her. He thanks Elenia, then learns that Nienna has died while he was gone.

Recovery brings pain, fogginess and worry that his music has changed. When Saray visits with food, he fears losing the part of himself that makes other people smile. She reassures him; they promise that if one of them dies, the other still has a life to live. Dale also gives his husks toward Nienna’s return and argues for larger hunting parties. Being brought home changes what he asks the company to do next.

Nienna’s final choice

Dale sings courage into the defenders around Hope and is present for Nienna’s final sacrifice. Nienna says goodbye to “sweet Dale.” His answer preserves both admiration and unease instead of declaring that her death was simply correct.

You’re foolish, Miss Nienna, but oh so brave.Dale

Care that does not seize the mind

After Nienna’s death, Saray blames herself. Dale supports her while recognizing that he cannot simply argue her out of guilt. He tells Adelia that Saray must reach the realization herself that nothing could have been done.

Saray: a life worth coming home to

Dale’s attachment to Saray begins in the early expeditions, where concern for her safety makes his already hesitant speech stumble. In August he notices what restores her happiness: “They make you smile again. That makes them precious.” Affection is expressed through attention, music, and reassurance.

They marry on 11 October 2024. Gartina makes a cake inspired by a hay bale, a shared memory later exploited by impostors. In August 2025 Dale resists supernatural allure by centering Saray: “Nothing can allure Dale since he met Saray!”

His readiness to give his life also frightens her. Loyalty can preserve their shared life or threaten to take him out of it; the tension remains part of their relationship.

The loss that reveals the community

During the battle recorded on 16 November 2024 locally, or 17 November UTC, Dale falls after standing against a doomcaller. Wren weeps while helping the living; Arjahn pleads for divine aid; friends give their farewells. Their reactions show how much of their imagined future already includes him.

The return happens within that same battle. Elenia reaches Dale with a burst of light and an indignant hoof-stomp. Gartina sees him come back to life; Dale smiles at Saray, dazed but responsive. Wren is stunned to see him standing again.

Relief does not erase the other losses. Dale sees the companions still down and asks why he was the one brought back. The scene establishes Elenia’s action and his restored life, without supplying the exact spell name or making his return a guarantee for anyone else.

Gartina, the wedding, and immediate loyalty

During the 2025 search for the real Gartina, impostors invoke Dale’s wedding and the cake Gartina made for it as evidence of intimacy. Those memories are credible because Dale and Gartina share a mundane social history deep enough to become an identity test. When he understands that she has been taken, his reasoning becomes direct: “These things took Gartina. Dale smash.” The phrasing is funny; the loyalty is absolute.

Ridiculous without becoming disposable

Dale becomes a shark during an underwater danger, successfully hides behind a potted plant, and feels private relief when directions are explicit enough to spare him from revealing trouble with left and right. His jokes, awkwardness and improvised solutions continue during dangerous events.

Dale speaks plainly about affection and danger. Even when he has no explanation for the cosmology or politics around him, he recognizes a friend in trouble and acts. He uses the same direct language for serious moments and jokes.

Gael’s practical work

In the refugee settlement, Dale helps turn emergency survival toward civic continuity: food, eating tools, permanent housing, salvaged lumber, and direct consultation. The actions are humble beside Gael’s divine history, but they are how liberation becomes a place people can inhabit.

Ordinary affection as world history

Dale’s wedding, shared meals, travel, jokes, rescues, and familiar habits give the adventurers a civilian life beneath their battles. When he is lost, the force of Arjahn’s desperation and Wren’s grief measures years of accumulated affection more clearly than any formal title could. Other people’s reactions establish the value Dale never needs to announce for himself.

Dale’s place in the company rests on the life his friends share with him: music, meals, a wedding, jokes and his willingness to help. Their grief when he falls, and relief when he returns, make those ties visible alongside what he can do in a fight.

The incomplete chronology

The recovered history now connects Dale’s May 2024 arrival, his July restoration, marriage, November loss and immediate return, and later practical work. His two returns have direct scenes, while the precise spell names and parts of his wider travels remain incomplete.

His history accumulates through companionship: a song, a promise, a rescue, a meal and the work of making somewhere to live. Those acts give his friends reasons to imagine him beside them when the next danger comes.

Trust tested in Akarian’s training

The encounter recorded on 12 October 2024 (UTC) is an Akarian training exercise. Dale tells Saray he trusts her lead, but an enemy takes control of him and commands him to attack her. Saray fights to break that control and reassures him that the war needs him. The exercise ends in defeat, with Dale down and Saray unconscious. Akarian heals them and brings them out, warning that the opponents targeted their concern for each other, Saray’s reliance on blindsight, and their inability to stop spells. This is a lesson survived, not a Babel battlefield death.

Safety requires more than fighting

Dale borrows a farmer’s plow to make a drainage ditch and asks Pappy for help with the harness. Pappy’s first question is where the water will go; Dale has not decided. Elsewhere, Alyhotep and Olokun discuss growing demand on resources and the need for infrastructure, trade and organization. These scenes show practical problems being worked through, not a completed drainage system or an enacted economic program.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

Scenes in sequence

These selected scenes track choices, knowledge and consequences. Dates identify UTC source postings; later status is not inferred from an absence.

  1. 2024-07-09 · compatible RP

    Waking to another friend’s loss

    Elenia restores Dale at the Tower; he wakes beside Saray and learns that Nienna has died.

    Known at this stage
    The needed diamond has been used on Dale; Nienna’s restoration is still a future effort.
    Consequence
    His survival leads into gratitude, guilt and practical help obtaining another diamond.
    Still unresolved
    The exact spell name is not established by these selected records.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5

  2. 2024-07-10 · compatible RP

    A promise that leaves room for the survivor

    Dale and Saray discuss his changed music and promise that the survivor still has a life to live. He contributes to Nienna’s recovery effort.

    Known at this stage
    Both know that the expedition can kill them; they cannot promise permanent safety.
    Consequence
    Affection becomes mutual permission to continue living and a proposal for safer hunting groups.
    Still unresolved
    Their words do not establish that grief or self-blame is finished.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6

  3. 2024-11-17 · quest

    A return within the battle

    After Dale falls, Elenia reaches him with light; he returns to life and responds to Saray.

    Known at this stage
    The company has already begun mourning him and other companions remain in danger.
    Consequence
    The recovered return precedes his later appearances by months; his relief coexists with guilt about the fallen.
    Still unresolved
    The exact spell and a universal rule of revival are not established.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3 · Receipt 4 · Receipt 5 · Receipt 6 · Receipt 7

  4. 2025-03-04 · quest

    A future with music and a home

    Saray gives Dale a gift and speaks of hearing his music if he builds in Gael.

    Known at this stage
    Building is a plan they can imagine after the war’s immediate losses.
    Consequence
    Their relationship includes ordinary hopes as well as farewells and rescues.
    Still unresolved
    The exchange does not establish a completed house or identify the gift’s magical properties.

    Receipt 1 · Receipt 2 · Receipt 3

A map, a snake and an uncertain leader

Before the Old Earth Hills expedition, Dale has bought more mapping supplies than he knows how to use. Montefucco has taught him to read a simple map, but making one is new work. He asks Olokun for a plan, fumbles with the equipment, then surprises himself by telling the company it is time to leave.

His preparations include a smaller responsibility: if something happens to him, he asks Wren to feed the baby rat snake in his tavern room. He has promised Saray he will look after it. Wren agrees, and the company sets out.

At the end, Dale insists that the dangerous cave must stay closed to protect anyone who might wander in. When others keep debating, he dismisses himself as a poor leader. Olokun answers with the result: they completed the mission and no one died. Wren adds that sealing the cave saved them. Their reassurance comes after the work, while Dale is still doubting it.

Soup before the settlement plan

Dale comes down from the Tower to ask how the refugees are holding up, then joins Gartina in preparing soup. He peels and chops carrots, quietly checking a few pieces are bite-sized by eating them. Turning to the onions, he braces for tears while the conversation turns toward permanent shelter.

He proposes salvaging the wrecked ship for a longhouse if it cannot be repaired. He also asks whether anyone has spoken properly to the refugees or found out who represents them. The building idea needs their participation. His joking suggestion that the ship’s mast would make a splendid circus tent belongs beside that practical question.

The cooking conversation also carries his uncertainty about the future. He says he will go where Saray goes and worries that he holds his friends back. He wants to clear fiends from the Plains, but no longer considers going alone sensible. Food, shelter and a safer next expedition are being discussed by someone who still needs reassurance himself.

relationshipMap.title: Dale’s relationship web
relationshipMap.intro: Dale’s importance accumulates through meals, jokes, weddings, rescues, and immediate loyalty. Select a tie to see how ordinary affection becomes part of the world’s history.

nodes.title: Nienna
nodes.subtitle: Goodbye to sweet Dale
nodes.history: Dale sings courage into the defenders around Hope and witnesses Nienna’s final sacrifice. She says goodbye to ‘sweet Dale’; he calls her foolish and brave.
nodes.consequence: His response preserves affection, admiration, and unease together. Love does not require him to pretend that her death was simple or painless.
nodes.evidence: The farewell and Dale’s reply are directly preserved.

nodes.title: Saray
nodes.subtitle: Care without seizing her grief
nodes.history: After Nienna’s death, Saray blames herself. Dale remains beside her and tells Adelia that Saray must reach for herself the realization that nothing could have been done.
nodes.consequence: He refuses both abandonment and forced reassurance. His care recognizes that closeness does not give him control over another person’s grief.
nodes.evidence: Saray’s guilt and Dale’s support are established; their wider chronology remains partial.

nodes.title: Gartina
nodes.subtitle: Cake, relief work, and rescue
nodes.relation: Mundane history becomes an identity test
nodes.history: Gartina makes the cake for Dale’s wedding and later works beside him feeding Gael’s refugees. Impostors use those memories because the ordinary history is credible enough to test belonging.
nodes.consequence: When Gartina is taken, Dale’s response is immediate: rescue her. Their relationship proves that shared domestic and civic life can carry as much historical weight as a battlefield oath.
nodes.evidence: Wedding, cake, Gael work, and rescue response are established; the full friendship remains incomplete.

nodes.title: Arjahn
nodes.subtitle: Desperation after Dale falls
nodes.history: Dale’s apparent death drives Arjahn toward an extraordinarily dangerous rescue and then toward anger at Bahamut when divine aid does not come.
nodes.consequence: Arjahn’s response measures Dale’s social importance more clearly than any formal rank. Ordinary companionship has become something he cannot accept losing quietly.
nodes.evidence: The grief and rescue response are established; Elenia’s immediate restoration is now recovered, while its exact spell name remains unestablished.

nodes.title: Wren
nodes.subtitle: Tears, healing, and remembered death
nodes.relation: Grief carried while another life is saved
nodes.history: Wren cries when Dale falls and immediately heals Arjahn. Dale’s return within the battle shocks her because she has already started carrying him as one of the dead.
nodes.consequence: The bond joins grief to continued action. Dale matters not because he dominates the scene, but because the group’s imagined future already includes him.
nodes.evidence: Wren’s reactions are established; the broader friendship remains partly recovered.

nodes.title: Gael’s refugees
nodes.subtitle: People, not a logistics problem
nodes.history: Dale helps provide soup, bowls, spoons, lumber, and shelter, then asks whether anyone has actually consulted the displaced people about permanent settlement.
nodes.consequence: The question limits benevolent ownership. Caring for people’s survival does not grant the company authority to decide their future without them.
nodes.evidence: The relief work and consultation question are established; the settlement’s later outcome remains incomplete.

insights.label: Foundational farewell
insights.note: Bravery and foolishness can remain true together.

insights.note: Other people reveal how much ordinary life had formed around him.

insights.label: Character method
insights.note: When a friend is endangered, help the friend.

profile.personality: Dale is funny without being emotionally disposable. He turns into a shark, hides behind a potted plant, struggles with directions, and still recognizes the truth that matters fastest: when a friend is in danger, help the friend. His simplicity is an emotionally competent way of belonging, not proof that nothing inside him is serious.
profile.achievements: He sings courage into Hope’s defenders, helps Gael’s refugees move from emergency food toward permanent settlement, and accumulates enough ordinary history that his apparent death shakes the entire company. His wedding, journeys, jokes, and practical work make community itself one of his achievements.
profile.relationships: Gartina’s place in Dale’s life is preserved through the wedding cake and the fury her abduction produces. Arjahn’s desperate rescue plan and crisis of faith, Wren’s grief while healing the living, Nienna’s affectionate farewell, and Saray’s trusted grief all show how much social weight Dale carries without needing to announce it.
